model_gate.reason: No comparable as-published multi-cycle turnout features with validated incremental forecast gain. Historical 'returned' can include in-person ballots. Registration and timing cannot identify candidate preference.
model_gate.required: Comparable ballot modes, publication timestamps, days-before-election alignment, and held-out cycle Brier/MAE improvement over polls.

references.name: North Carolina State Board of Elections

recency_experiment.design: 21/30/45-day half-lives; identical expanding-cycle training; office selection at nearest current horizon; outer decay selection uses earlier cycles only.
recency_experiment.scope: Historical poll-model races only; not current rating priors, markets, early vote corrections or 2026 accuracy. No production parameter is changed here.

publication_lag_experiment.design: Three days of conservative delay after fieldwork ends, applied consistently to historical training and held-out snapshots. Compare identical races at the nearest current horizon with nested office-model selection.
publication_lag_experiment.scope: A delay assumption is a sensitivity analysis, not recovered publication history. Backfilled/revised data can have longer delays. Live forecasts remain unchanged; actual as-published timestamps are the preferred future input.

house_control_validation.design: National generic-ballot forecasts and seat curves trained on earlier cycles only. Fixed poll model avoids choosing a model with future labels.
house_control_validation.scope: Only a few independent chamber outcomes are available, especially with the production post-2012 curve. These results do not validate historical district rating priors or certify the live market context layer.

research_audit.scope: Nested earlier-cycle model selection, limited to House, Senate and governors. No presidential races, national generic-ballot outcomes, unpolled rating priors or markets.

paired_weighted_poll_comparison.resampling_unit: entire election cycle; race-weighted paired Brier difference
paired_weighted_poll_comparison.scope: Few heterogeneous election cycles; exploratory uncertainty, not proof of superiority.

complexity_guard_experiment.design: Require at least 80 earlier office races, three earlier cycles and 0.002 earlier Brier gain before allowing the selected policy over weighted polls.

comparison_with_selected_policy.resampling_unit: entire election cycle; race-weighted paired Brier difference
comparison_with_selected_policy.scope: Few heterogeneous election cycles; exploratory uncertainty, not proof of superiority.

complexity_guard_experiment.decision: No production switch: the guard worsened held-out Brier. Neither complexity nor simplicity is adopted merely on intuition.

questions.question: Does winning an independent seat imply caucus control?
questions.decision: No. MT is a multiway comparison, NE affiliation is unresolved; publish conditional caucus stress endpoints, not invented independent win/caucus probabilities.

questions.question: Does a reused district number preserve its historical electorate?
questions.decision: No. Verified TX-09 boundary change retires the old district vote prior. Other remapped districts still require comparable reconstructed baselines.

questions.question: Does overall accuracy hide competitive-race difficulty?
questions.decision: Report close-race and safe-race scores separately. Outcome-defined close subsets are retrospective diagnostics, not a deployable selection rule.

questions.question: Are hundreds of races hundreds of independent error realizations?
questions.decision: No. Compare matched races using whole-cycle bootstrap; inspect the interval before claiming improvement.

questions.question: Can fieldwork end be treated as public availability?
questions.decision: Only as a documented limitation where publication is unknown. Enforce verified release dates, retain first-observed source versions and publish a three-day delay sensitivity.

questions.question: Can a generic-ballot archive be appended without source replacement?
questions.decision: No. Replace office/cycle coverage cells to prevent double weighting; keep older uncovered history.

questions.question: Do registered Democrats voting early identify net Democratic votes?
questions.decision: No. Registration, vote choice, mode substitution and reporting lag differ. Early-vote data remains visible with zero central probability weight pending validated comparable history.

questions.question: Are pollster labels independent organizations or samples?
questions.decision: No. An eight-way ablation separates alias pooling of frequency caps, counts and prior-cycle bias. The earlier-cycle-only outer policy does not establish an improvement, so production defaults remain unchanged. Publisher, sponsor, fieldwork and panel identities need separate provenance.

correlation_experiment.design: Fixed correlations 0/.15/.30/.45 plus an earlier-cycle selection rule. Evaluate predictive count distributions using ranked probability loss.
correlation_experiment.scope: Historical poll-covered Senate/governor subsets with at least five contests; not full chambers, not caucus-aligned control or validation of unpolled priors. Few cycles and changing poll coverage limit generalization. No production rho change.

pollster_identity_experiment.design: Eight-way factorial ablation of alias pooling for frequency caps, organization counts and prior-cycle house effects. Reported labels and outcomes remain intact. Policy selection uses earlier cycles only, with the same nested office/model selection inside each identity policy.

paired_comparison.resampling_unit: entire election cycle; race-weighted paired Brier difference
paired_comparison.scope: Few heterogeneous election cycles; exploratory uncertainty, not proof of superiority.

outer_paired_comparison.resampling_unit: entire election cycle; race-weighted paired Brier difference
outer_paired_comparison.scope: Few heterogeneous election cycles; exploratory uncertainty, not proof of superiority.

pollster_identity_experiment.scope: Alias-normalized organization keys are not a count of statistically independent polls. Publisher, sponsor, fieldwork, panel and weighting roles differ. No live probabilities or production parameters changed by this script.

independent_caucus_sensitivity.interpretation: Stress endpoints: all unresolved seats contribute zero or one D-aligned seat each. These are neither a confidence interval nor estimates of independent candidate win/caucus probabilities.

control.model_type: historically calibrated House seats-vote simulation plus correlated latent-normal Senate/Governor race simulation

assumptions.why_not_independent: National and office shocks let Senate/Governor errors move races together; House aggregate uncertainty comes from historical seats-vote and generic-ballot forecast errors.

sensitivity.method: Use the least/most Democratic listed matchup in each race and shift every unvalidated external-rating prior by -/+5 probability points.
sensitivity.interpretation: Stress range, not a statistical confidence interval.

control.important_limit: Race-rating fallback probabilities remain provisional. House totals now receive a national calibration with sparse held-out chamber evidence; individual unpolled district probabilities are still not direct poll-model outputs.

house_national_calibration.interpretation: House totals use the historical national seats-vote curve because district polling is sparse; polled districts remain unchanged and only fallback rating priors are raked to the national expectation.

prediction_market_context.method: De-vig each market, pool sources in log-odds space, then cap chamber-level influence at 15% and any displayed shift at five probability points.

house.interpretation: External reasonableness reference only; it does not replace the coherent seat simulation or count as an independently backtested model input.

senate.interpretation: External reasonableness reference only; it does not replace the coherent seat simulation or count as an independently backtested model input.

races.multi_candidate_warning: The opposition candidate is independent. Candidate win probability does not establish Senate caucus affiliation; central control uses an aligned proxy.
Competitive independent candidate(s): Seth Bodnar. The two-side model does not estimate the full three-way winner probability.

authenticity.fec_match_note: Name-compatible filings are not identity, ballot qualification or nomination proof. Unresolved nicknames are review flags, not invalid candidates.

model_card.validation: strict expanding-window walk-forward by election cycle
model_card.training_rule: each held-out cycle is predicted using earlier cycles only
model_card.probability_calibration: A partially pooled logistic calibrator is double-gated by later cycles and model-level Brier gain; it remains identity when the gain is under 0.001.
model_card.important_scope_note: Metrics apply only to historical poll-model snapshots; external rating priors used for unpolled current races are not included.
